Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Zenith Insurance Group Third Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. We will prioritize questions from analysts, and instructions will be provided at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Zenith Insurance Group's Third Quarter 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Mark Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer; David Patel, Chief Underwriting Officer; Robert Kline, Chief Investment Officer; Jennifer Hayes, Chief Operating Officer; and Michael Grant, Chief Claims Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we are making today may be considered forward-looking. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause our actual results to differ materially from those projected. We encourage you to review our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks and uncertainties.

I will now turn the call over to Mark Reynolds.

Mark Reynolds: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on Zenith Insurance Group's performance for the third quarter. We delivered strong results, driven by robust new business production, solid net written premium growth across lines of business, effective management of catastrophe losses, a highly efficient reinsurance program, favorable impacts from pricing adjustments on premium volumes, positive realized and unrealized gains in our investment portfolio, and a fortified capital position with elevated statutory surplus levels. We are making significant progress on our digital transformation initiatives, including AI-enhanced underwriting and claims processing.

Lisa, our CFO, will now provide a more detailed review of our financial performance.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, Mark. Good morning, everyone. As Mark mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Our net income was $525 million, or $2.15 per share. Key drivers of our financial performance included resilient underwriting amid elevated catastrophe activity, disciplined pricing that boosted premium volumes, strong new business momentum, favorable investment returns, an optimized reinsurance structure, steady NWP expansion by segment, and prudent capital management.

Let me dive deeper into these elements, starting with total catastrophe losses impact, which remains a volatile but critical factor in our property and casualty results. Cat losses represent insured losses from major natural and man-made events, net of reinsurance recoveries. For Q3 2024, our total catastrophe losses reached $1.35 billion, up approximately 45% from $930 million in Q3 2023, equating to 8.2% of gross written premium compared to 5.2% last year. Year-to-date through September 30th, we're at $3.1 billion in cat losses, or 6.8% of year-to-date GWP of $45.6 billion. This is our heaviest quarterly cat load since Q3 2021's Hurricane Ida event, which hit 9.5% of GWP, well above our five-year average quarterly cat ratio of 4.5%.

By peril and region, in the U.S., accounting for 58% of our P&C GWP, cats totaled $790 million in Q3—mainly from Hurricane Helene's impact in the Southeast and expanded California wildfires. Helene generated $480 million in gross claims across homeowners and commercial multi-peril, dominated by wind and surge, netting to 5.4% of U.S. P&C GWP after reinsurance. Wildfires contributed $200 million, focused on high-value properties in the West, where drier conditions have widened claims perimeters, similar to 2020's major fire seasons affecting competitors.

Internationally, Europe added $310 million from convective storms and flooding in Germany and the Benelux region, echoing 2021's Ahr Valley events but with higher insured shares via our motor and SME portfolios. Asia-Pacific contributed $170 million from Typhoon Yagi analogs in Japan and the Philippines, hitting facultative reinsurance. Man-made cats, such as Maui wildfire spillovers into liability, added $60 million, now comprising 13% of total cats versus 9% last year.

This activity elevated our P&C combined ratio to 103.1%, with cat-driven loss ratios at 69.2% versus 62.8% ex-cat. Excluding cats, attritional loss ratios improved 110 basis points year-over-year to 57.9%, thanks to pricing discipline and enhanced claims handling. Reinsurance recoveries totaled $475 million in Q3, capping net retention at 36% via quota share and excess-of-loss layers with Swiss Re and Munich Re. Our retrocession, tied to RMS v19 models, worked as modeled, though we note risks from correlated wind perils.

We're responding aggressively: accelerating cat modeling with our Zenith Cat Platform, now covering 85% of the portfolio and using CMIP6 climate data for tail-risk tuning. This drove 13-16% rate hikes on U.S. homeowners renewals from October 1, closing an 9% book-to-market gap in coastal areas. Parametric pilots with RenaissanceRe in Florida for hurricane wind have disbursed $28 million seamlessly, cutting disputes by 38%. We're trimming Southeast U.S. exposure by 8% through non-renewals while expanding 12% in low-cat Midwest commercial. Reinsurance now includes more ILS from Twelve Capital for diversification.

For Q4, we anticipate cats at 5.5-6.5% of GWP per NOAA's above-average season outlook, with full-year at 6.4%, in our 5-7% band, supporting mid-single-digit ex-cat ROE growth and a 255% combined RBC ratio, alongside a $550 million buyback authorization.

Turning to the effectiveness of our reinsurance program, which has been a strategic pillar for capital protection and earnings stability. For the first nine months of 2024, gross written premiums rose 9.1% to $5.2 billion, with ceded premiums at $1.45 billion—a 27.8% ceded ratio, down 35 basis points year-over-year—yielding net written premiums of $3.75 billion. This efficiency improved net loss ratios to 61.8%, a 190 basis points gain, and a calendar-year combined ratio of 94.8% ex-cats, in our 93-97% target.

Our multi-layered program for our $16.5 billion in-force book features quota shares—26% on U.S. P&C and 21% on international casualty, ceding $950 million year-to-date with A+ rated partners. Cat XoL towers renewed January 1 at stable rates post-Helene and wildfires, with a $550 million all-peril layer at $160 million retention, 2x reinstatements, via Swiss Re, Munich Re, RenaissanceRe, and $350 million collateralized from Stone Ridge and Fermat.

ILWs and collateralized layers added $220 million, triggering $50 million from Helene-like events for liquidity. Recoveries hit $680 million year-to-date, a 97.5% rate on paid losses, up from prior year—key in absorbing 74% of Q3's $290 million net cats, limiting net PML to 1.3% of surplus versus gross 4.3% per RMS v19.

Regionally adaptive: U.S. $9.2 billion TIV geo-capped in Florida/Texas, renewed flat post-hardening using KCC models. Europe Perils indices yielded $35 million from Storm analogs; Asia $110 million Japan tower retaining 11% net.

We've upgraded modeling with RMS/AIR hybrids and ML, cutting gross loss estimates 13%; piloting $160 million cat bond via ZenithRe at 6.7% coupon. Net PML under 14% of surplus, costs at 4.1% of ceded—below NAIC peers—freeing $500 million capital for growth, at 185% RBC.

July renewals secured 2.5% rate-on-line; expanding ILS to 22% by 2025 for $60 million savings.

Next, our capital position and statutory surplus levels, a foundation of our strength. As of September 30, consolidated statutory surplus was $19.8 billion, up 12% year-over-year from $17.7 billion, fueled by operating earnings, fixed income gains from Fed hikes, and reserve releases in workers' comp and auto. Organic growth ex-Q2 rebalancing ($480 million gain) was 8%.

RBC ratio at 390% consolidated, up from 368% last year—elite vs. Travelers' 285%, Chubb's 325%. P&C at 415%, life/annuity 345%. Investment income $680 million in Q3, +24% YoY at 5.0% yield (66% IG corporates/munis, 19% Treasuries, 15% alts). Offset $410 million cat losses (2.7% GWP), combined 93.1%.

U.S. $13.4 billion surplus (68%), 400% NAIC RBC; Europe €3.4 billion at 202% Solvency II; Asia-Pacific $2.4 billion +17%, 325% RBC.

Initiatives: $1.3 billion quota share freed $850 million RBC; FIA growth 20% to $4.8 billion; ERM with AI stress tests >255% RBC in extreme cats. $550 million buyback (2.3 million shares at $152), dividends $0.90/share +11%, 36% payout. Targeting cyber/D&O M&A, $350 million insurtech/parametrics.

Now, new business production volume, measured via annualized premium equivalent (APE) and policy counts. Q3 2024 new APE $3.0 billion, +19% YoY from $2.52 billion—strongest in years. New policies 1.55 million, +23% from 1.26 million, via commercial shift and digital channels.

P&C $2.05 billion APE (68%), +27%: Personal auto $920 million +16%, 1% share gain via DriveSafe telematics (38% mix, 22% lower LR); homeowners $450 million +22%, 47% bundling. Commercial $680 million +41%, 195,000 SMB policies via QuickBooks APIs.

Life/Health $950 million +6%, 380,000 policies, 27% embedded (e.g., Walmart-like).

U.S. 78% ($2.34 billion +21%); Europe $480 million +13%; APAC $260 million +9%, India micro-ins.

Drivers: GenAI underwriting (85% P&C, 42% faster binds), 15% pricing, 12% agency growth. Headwinds: insurtech pressure, cats. Q4 $3.1-3.3 billion APE, full-year $12.5-13 billion, 17-21% growth.

On net written premiums growth by line: Q3 NWP +9.8% YoY, from 8.2% Q2, beating 8.5% guide. Personal Lines (42%) +8.1% to $3.0 billion: auto +6.7% on 6.3% rates, ApexDrive 1.3 million users; homeowners +13.1% amid perils, 97.5% CR.

Commercial (36%) +11.5% to $4.4 billion: WC +12.2%, ApexWork AI; property +13.8%, 10% rates; GL +9.3%. Specialty (17%) +16.2% to $2.0 billion: cyber +23.7%, ApexCyber 93% attach; D&O +12.8%.

Life/Health (5%) +4.7% to $580 million. U.S. 84% growth; initiatives: GenAI full rollout, $2.2 billion capacity unlock. Earned rates +8.6%.

Regarding the impact of pricing changes on premium volume, NWP grew 8.7% to $4.0 billion on 10.2% earned rates, vs. industry 6.5%, combined 93.2%. Personal auto 13.1% hikes drove 10.9% growth despite 0.5% policy dip, UBI 30% mix. Homeowners 11.8% rates, +10.4%, parametrics 17%.

Commercial WC 15.4%, GL/E&S 17.1%, premiums +12.8%, 92% retention. U.S. 11.2% rates/11.1% growth; Europe 6.1%; APAC/LatAm 10.3%.

'Profit First' analytics on 550 million claims; retention 90.2%. Q4 10.5-11.5% rates.

Investment income $350 million. Portfolio $158 billion: realized gains $230 million (+48%), equities $150 million, fixed rotations $90 million, duration 5.7 years. Unrealized +$115 million, AOCI -$2.1 billion. Fixed -$130 million recovery; initiatives: swaps, CDS, ESG. Full-year $900 million gains.

Our combined ratio was 96.5%. We continue to maintain a strong capital position, with 285% RBC. Expense ratio improved to 27.9%.

David Patel: Thank you, Lisa. I'd like to provide an update on our underwriting performance. We've seen continued strong performance in our commercial property and casualty lines. We are actively managing our exposure to catastrophe risks and have implemented several initiatives to improve our risk selection, including advanced AI-driven modeling and parametric products, which have enhanced our pricing adequacy and retention in high-hazard areas.

Robert Kline: Thank you. From an investment perspective, we have continued to focus on diversifying our portfolio and managing risk in the current market environment. We are seeing positive returns from our investments in high-grade fixed income and alternatives, with proactive duration management and credit hedging supporting stable yields amid rate volatility.

Michael Grant: I'd like to briefly address our claims performance. We've implemented several initiatives to streamline our claims process and improve customer satisfaction, including digital platforms and telematics integration. We are seeing positive results in terms of reduced claims processing times, down 35% year-over-year, and higher net promoter scores.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: Thank you. Instructions for queuing questions. Our first question comes from Alex Rivera with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Good morning. Can you provide more color on the new business production trends and how they tie into your pricing strategy?

Mark Reynolds: Good morning, Alex. Absolutely. As Lisa detailed, our new APE hit $3.0 billion in Q3, up 19%, with policy counts surging 23%. This reflects our pricing discipline—10-15% hikes across lines—balanced by digital tools like InstantQuote, capturing 62% of personal new business. We're prioritizing profitable growth, with commercial leading at 41% gains via SMB focus, positioning us for sustained mid-teens expansion without sacrificing margins.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Carter with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter: Good morning. Could you discuss the impact of elevated catastrophe activity on your business?

Lisa Chen: Good morning, Emily. The $1.35 billion in Q3 cats, at 8.2% of GWP, was a headwind, but our reinsurance absorbed 64%, and ex-cat underwriting improved markedly. Pricing responses—13-16% on renewals—and exposure reductions in high-risk zones kept us resilient, with full-year cats in guidance and ROE growth intact.

Operator: Our next question comes from Jordan Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Jordan Lee: What is the expected impact of potential regulatory changes on your underwriting strategy?

David Patel: Good morning, Jordan. Regulatory scrutiny, like Florida reforms or Solvency II tweaks, is factored in. We're adapting via de-risking—8% Southeast trim—and tech like GenAI for compliant, precise underwriting. Our specialty growth in cyber/D&O remains insulated, with capacity discipline ensuring we thrive amid changes.

Operator: Our next question comes from Taylor Brooks with Bank of America. Please go ahead.

Taylor Brooks: Thanks. On the reinsurance front, how effective was it against this quarter's cats, and outlook for renewals?

Lisa Chen: Great question, Taylor. Recoveries were outstanding at 97.5% rate, capping net PML low. January renewals locked favorable terms; we'll expand ILS for cost efficiency, targeting below-industry costs while maintaining robust protection.

Operator: Thank you. That concludes the question portion. I'll now turn it back to Mark Reynolds for closing remarks.

Mark Reynolds: Thank you for your questions and your interest in Zenith Insurance Group. In closing, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders, backed by our tech investments, pricing power, and risk management. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
